newsitem.title: CANADA: Hearings seen on Alcan Quebec smelter plan.
newsitem.headline: Hearings seen on Alcan Quebec smelter plan.

text.p: A C$1.5 billion smelter project being mulled by Alcan Aluminium Ltd at its facilities in Alma, Quebec will undergo public hearings on its potential environmental impact, a Quebec government agency said on Wednesday.

The Bureau d'audiences publiques sur l'environnement du Quebec (BAPE) said hearings would begin on June 9 and a final report would be ready by the autumn. The hearings would not delay the project's timetable, the agency said.
Alcan has not given the official go-ahead for the project, and has said that it would make a decision at the end of this year or next year on whether to proceed.
The Alma project would include a new 350,000 metric ton smelter, which eventually would replace existing smelting capacity at Alcan facilities there.
Alma is about 186 miles (300 km) north of Quebec City.
If the project went ahead, it would be completed by 2000 or 2001 and employ 600 people.
The hearings will examine the technologies proposed for the smelter project, as well as plans to ensure air quality, public security and proper waste treatment and disposal.
